text.p: - A new tax on people and vehicles crossing Russia's boader is expected to be approved by the government in the next three months, boader guard officials say.
- Kazakhstan, the biggest former Soviet republic after Russia, is selling former Soviet industrial giants on its territory off cheap to Western investors to fill the budget gap.
- The range of weapons allowed to be used for self-defence has been extended according to a law signed by president Boris Yeltsin on December 13.
- The Red Cross shootings in Chechnya are a well planned and professionaly implemented terrorist act with definite political goals.
- Boris Yeltsin is due to return to his Kremlin residence next week and is ready for firm action to fight economic crisis in the country, says president's spokesman on Tuesday.

- Alexander Lebed has won his suit against Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov and might expect a public retraction of charges that Lebed was plotting a "creeping coup" involving 1,500 Chechen fighters.
- Personal income taxes are to be raised to improve tax collection to the budget, says Finance Minister Alexander Livshits.
- The shooting of six Red Cross workers is a crime aimed at disrupting the peaceful settlement of the Chechen conflict.
- Russia's Interior Ministry has been given the right to collect taxes according to President Boris Yeltsin's new decree. The federal tax police were set up in 1992.
- We have relinquished our global claims and are concentrating our energy in the most important directions, says chief of Russia's intelligence service Vyacheslav Trubin.

- For the last two years Russia's Federal Security service, successor to Soviet-era KGB, has helped reveal cases of corruption involving more then 500 high ranking officials, including regional goveners.

- One must be blind and deaf to ignore the logic of the chain of crimes in Chechnya. Who is less interested in the stability in the region, asks the paper in connection with the shooting of the Red Cross workers.
